A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bregman decoding framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebText generation and GSM8K experiments, including accuracy, perplexity, repetition, MAUVE, and selected support sizes in Section 5 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds evaluations with Qwen and Phi, TriviaQA results, and further analyses of adaptive support sizes in Appendix H.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds an optional exponential-search procedure: try support bounds 1, 2, 4, and so forth, then perform binary search within the resulting bound. The decoding objectives, renormalization maps, and Appendix F pseudocode remain unchanged; adoption of this alternative in the experiments is not established.

E1.justification: v2 adds factual question answering on TriviaQA in Appendix H.4, extending coverage beyond the retained WebText generation and GSM8K mathematical reasoning tasks. This introduces a distinct task requirement, rather than merely another model configuration.

E2.justification: Standard top-k remains the evaluated comparator for primal Bregman decoding. The added Qwen and Phi models are evaluation backbones, and the new comparisons retain the same decoding-method membership. Other decoding methods remain discussed rather than evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct and Phi-3-medium-4k-instruct configurations and a TriviaQA protocol using 10% of the validation set, approximately 1,800 questions. Figure 9 reports absolute perplexity and repetition differences for the added models, and H.5 adds support-size variability and entropy measures. Existing experiments retain their settings.

E4.justification: H.5 extends the existing support-size analysis by reporting standard deviations and entropies, probing how much the selected k varies, and extending this analysis across models and tasks. The original mean-k table is retained as Table 11, formerly Table 2; the theoretical illustrations and temperature analysis in Appendix G are unchanged.

E5.justification: v2 supplements mean support sizes with newly reported standard deviations and entropies in H.5. These describe support-size variability, not uncertainty across repeated experimental runs. Performance uncertainty reporting remains based on 1,000 bootstrap resamples, or 50 for MAUVE, with no added seed or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Figure 9 and Tables 3–10 and 12–20 add extensive model, TriviaQA, and adaptivity results. For example, Table 6 reports Phi GSM8K accuracy of 72.25% versus matched top-k's 62.62% at temperature 1.5, lambda 0.0001, and alpha 1.5. Earlier results are unchanged: v1 Tables 1, 2, and 3 map to v2 Tables 1, 11, and 2, respectively.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 adds the complexity argument for exponential search, requiring O(log k*) tested support sizes and renormalizations over at most O(k*) coordinates. The principal definitions, assumptions, theorems, and proofs in Appendices A–G remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction newly makes an explicit novelty claim for an objective-based foundation of adaptive decoding, while the abstract explicitly claims logarithmic-time identification of k. The central contributions—sparse Bregman decoding, greedy optimality, discrete convexity, and recovering top-k as a special case—are retained.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly connects reduced repetition to increased weighting of smaller retained probabilities. Section 7 adds specific discussion of support-size scaling, the unresolved primal–dual relationship, extensions to other truncation rules, and possible applications beyond LLMs, replacing v1's brief discussion of future work.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added model variants, TriviaQA validation fraction and approximate sample count, and rounded support sizes used to configure additional top-k comparisons. Appendix F's implementation pseudocode and H.1's hardware and software details are unchanged, with no new code-access information.

R1.justification: The same 61 references are retained; bibliography changes are primarily capitalization corrections. Research positioning changes modestly through the introduction's explicit novelty claim for objective-based adaptivity and its broader placement of decoding among inference-time methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution roadmap, and computational explanation in Section 3 undergo substantial rewriting. Section 7 becomes a discussion organized around several specific directions, Appendix H gains dedicated subsections, and the redundant appendix contents list is removed.

P2.justification: v2 adds the four-panel Figure 9 and 17 additional tables covering performance and adaptivity. Existing figures are retained, the original mean-k table moves into H.5, and Table 1 and Figure 3 exchange display order. These materially expand and reorganize the empirical presentation.

improvement.justification: The additional model evaluations, TriviaQA results, and support-size variability analyses strengthen the empirical support for the framework, while rewritten explanations improve accessibility. The overall gain is limited: the foundational theory and earlier results are retained, and the added studies remain illustrative top-k comparisons with limited protocol detail for the new task.
